title: JVM Internals
objectives: Describe the JVM runtime memory areas
Explain class loading and JIT compilation
Read a stack trace and OutOfMemoryError types

sections.markdown: The JVM is the virtual machine that loads, verifies and executes Java bytecode, manages memory, and JIT-compiles hot code to native instructions.

sections.code:
JVM memory:
  Heap        -> objects (GC-managed): Young (Eden+Survivor) + Old
  Metaspace   -> class metadata (native memory, replaced PermGen in Java 8)
  Stack       -> one per thread: frames, locals, partial results
  PC register -> current instruction per thread
  Native stack-> JNI calls

sections.markdown:
## Class loading
- **Loading** → **Linking** (verify, prepare, resolve) → **Initialization**.
- Loaders are hierarchical: Bootstrap → Platform → Application, using parent-delegation.
JIT: the JVM starts interpreting bytecode, profiles 'hot' methods, then compiles them to optimized native code (C1/C2 tiers). This is why a long-running JVM gets faster over time (warm-up).
OutOfMemoryError flavors: 'Java heap space' (too many live objects), 'Metaspace' (too many classes), 'unable to create native thread' (thread/OS limit). The message tells you where to look.

flashcards.front: Heap vs stack in the JVM?
flashcards.back: Heap holds objects (shared, GC-managed); each thread has its own stack of frames with locals and call info.
Metaspace, which stores class metadata in native memory and grows dynamically.
Profiles hot methods and compiles them from bytecode to optimized native code at runtime.
